DisplayAnything 0.1.0, built by CI from `main` at [4dbf18c](https://github.com/ZGremlin/DisplayAnything/commit/4dbf18cfeee43fc968469c4d6a25029fe7fb3241) ([CI run](https://github.com/ZGremlin/DisplayAnything/actions/runs/45825650760)). The window footer shows build `4dbf18c`.

Setup, shortcuts and troubleshooting are in the [README on main](https://github.com/ZGremlin/DisplayAnything/blob/main/README.md).

## Downloads

| File | For |
| --- | --- |
| `DisplayAnything_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe` | Windows installer (tray app) |
| `DisplayAnything-macOS.zip` | macOS app (zipped `DisplayAnything.app`) |
| `DisplayAnythingInstall.sh` | macOS install helper: `bash ~/Downloads/DisplayAnythingInstall.sh ~/Downloads/DisplayAnything-macOS.zip` |
| `da-agent.exe`, `da-agent-macos.tar.gz` | Optional command-line agent |

The builds aren't signed. Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run (More info › Run anyway). On a Mac, use the install helper: it clears the quarantine flag, re-signs the app locally and opens the Accessibility and Screen Recording permission pages.

## What's in it

- **Pairing and connections:** pair two machines by IP with a 6-digit code; mutual TLS 1.3 with pinned certificates; saved devices reconnect on their own, including after a reboot or IP change; starts at login; tray app.
- **Keyboard and mouse sharing:** switch with a hotkey (changeable, including mouse buttons) or with edge crossing; an always-come-back shortcut; Ctrl/Command swap on the Mac; Windows keyboard-hook watchdog.
- **Shared clipboard:** text, images and files follow the keyboard and mouse when you switch (#4).
- **Remote screen control:** view and control the other computer's screen (#3), with a choice of resolution (the host really switches mode for the session and switches back) and quality; ultrawide screens are scaled to fit the encoder and smaller pictures show the whole screen instead of a corner (#5).

Not included yet: the iOS app and display takeover.
